text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - UK shares closed sharply higher on Monday, buoyed by the latest batch of subdued price data, which lessened the fear of an imminent rise in UK interest rates, and further helped by Friday's strong rebound on Wall Street. The FTSE 100 index closed at the day's best level, up 50.7 points at 4,107.3, and within reach of the December 31 high of 4,118.5.
FRANKFURT - German shares climbed further into record territory on Monday following Wall Street's higher end-of-week close and backed by a firm dollar and German debt market.

The DAX-30 index of leading German shares ended floor trade up 21.56 points at 2,954.95 after touching an all-time high of 2,961.25 earlier in the session. In post-bourse trade the index rose 40.97 to 2,956.78.

PARIS - The French stockmarket's CAC-40 index set a closing record of 2,361.27 points on Monday, surpassing the previous closing record of 2,355.93 set on February 2, 1994, the French stockmarkets association SBF said. The French blue chip index also set a new intraday high of 2,371.38 points, up from the previous high of 2,360.98.

ZURICH - Swiss shares came off intra-day peaks but still closed at record highs. Dealers said the market was split as banks were neglected while buying centred on cyclical shares. The broad SPI closed up 22.70 points to a record close of 2,549.31 after touching an intra-day all-time high of 2,550.89.

TOKYO - Japanese stocks rebounded sharply on Monday from last week's steep dive, with the key market average racking up a gain of more than 4.7 percent in volatile trading. Brokers said the advance was a technical recovery driven by a rebound in banking shares but that the market still lacked confidence in the economy. The market's key barometer, the Nikkei average of 225 leading issues, soared 815.14 points to finish at 18,118.79.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended on a strong note on Monday, boosted by solid gains in the banking sector, pared losses in property counters and a rebound in Japanese share prices, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed 97.71 points higher at 13,289.21.

SYDNEY - Australian shares discounted strong gains made by the Dow to close only marginally firmer on Monday, after bond markets softened on concerns over U.S. inflation and interest rates. The All Ordinaries index clambered only 3.7 points higher to 2,422.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares defied all predictions of a limited rally to surge forward on Monday, sparked by a surprise rally on Wall Street. Robust U.S. jobs growth in December had spread initial fears that the Dow would drop on Friday and South African shares had shed value. But the Dow stunned observers to close at a fourth record high, leaving the South African market seen as oversold. As soon as trade kicked off on Monday buyers poured into stocks and prices rose across the board. The all-share index rose 84 points to 6,758.6 as industrials added 91.4 points to 8,130.7. The gold index rose 38.4 points to 1,460.2.
